The 8th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals in St. Louis granted xAI’s request for an injunction, putting the law on hold for now. A lower court judge rejected the same bid last month, Reuters reported.

Minnesota’s anti-“nudification” law took effect Aug. 1. It bars website operators, software developers and others from letting users create realistic images showing an intimate body part not visible in an original photo of an identifiable person.
The company argues the measure curbs free speech protected by the U.S. Constitution.
Last month, U.S. District Judge Donovan Frank ruled that xAI had not shown it would suffer irreparable harm during the case. He also said the company waited too long to seek emergency relief.
The company disputed the delay finding on appeal. It said its
